label: Real run on this Mac's Docker Compose stack, with synthetic traffic from klaxon.traffic: synthetic data, a simulated provider, no real money. One fault from klaxon.faults, secret-rotation, was injected on purpose. The alert was raised by klaxon.alerts from what the stack showed. Klaxon's loop ran live on it, through Claude Code on Aravind's seat, offered one write action (rollback_deploy), which runs only if a person approves it at the gate, and stopped on diagnosed after 4 steps; any reply it got is a recorded response, not a simulation. The diagnosis was compared with the fault's recorded cause by a rule (klaxon.grading), not by a person or a model. Klaxon asked at the approval gate to act on its diagnosis; the request was approved with make approve (the request's id typed at a terminal), and the action ran: redeploy webhook-receiver: WEBHOOK_SECRET_VERSION v2 -> v1. Code, not the model, then verified it (klaxon.agent.verify): passed; the cause is removed, and the money is right. The fault's cause was removed by Klaxon: its rollback (Klaxon, approved request r-cc97) removed the cause, and the harness's clearing then found the good settings running, and changed nothing.

fault.name: secret-rotation
fault.title: The books stop catching up: our webhook receiver refuses every webhook
fault.cause: a deploy of the webhook receiver with a rotated secret the provider does not sign with (WEBHOOK_SECRET_VERSION=v2, while the provider signs with v1): every webhook fails its signature check and is refused with a 400, so no event reaches Kafka, and the provider keeps sending them again, with backoff
expected_symptoms: the books cannot catch up with the provider: the money check cannot settle, the provider's webhooks not acknowledged, and the books rule fires at its second evaluation, about 50 s after the deploy
the receiver refuses every webhook with a 400, counts it as bad_signature and logs 'webhook refused: bad signature'; the provider sends its growing backlog again and again, tens of times a second
nothing new is booked or confirmed, and both consumers' lag stays at 0: nothing reaches Kafka

payments and refunds still go through, but one whose answer was lost cannot be confirmed: its client's retries get 503 again, so the 5xx share of POST /payments about doubles and its p95 climbs to about 0.6 s, both under their thresholds

after the rollback the books catch up within about two minutes: the provider sends each refused webhook again within a minute of its last try, and one whose acknowledgement is then lost (the traffic's noise) a minute later
fault.remedy: roll the webhook receiver back to v1 (or accept both versions until the provider signs with v2): the provider sends every refused webhook again, and the books catch up by themselves

diagnosis.hypothesis: webhook-receiver was redeployed at 02:50:46Z with WEBHOOK_SECRET_VERSION=v2. Since then it has rejected every provider webhook as bad_signature, at about 12/s and rising. The rate rises because the provider keeps resending webhooks that are not acknowledged. The provider seems to still sign with the earlier secret, so the receiver neither acknowledges these webhooks nor puts them on provider-events. Neither consumer books or confirms them. The money check cannot settle to its cutoff, and unacknowledged webhooks pile up (156 at the alert), which fires BooksBehindProvider.

evidence.shows: webhook-receiver is the only service changed after the 02:49:04Z stack start. It was recreated at 02:50:46Z with WEBHOOK_SECRET_VERSION=v2, about 50 s before the alert fired.

No bad_signature series exists before 02:50:58. It then appears and climbs from 1.4/s to 12.4/s. Over the same window the queued rate stops rising at 2.24/s and falls to 1.52/s. Few or no new webhooks are being queued since the deploy.
The receiver logs no WARN or ERROR lines for these rejections. The failure produces no warnings, so only the metric shows it.

proposed_fix.summary: Roll webhook-receiver back to its settings before the 02:50:46Z deploy, which used the earlier webhook secret version, so it accepts the provider's signatures again. The provider keeps resending unacknowledged webhooks, so the backlog should drain without a replay. Afterwards, run money_check with wait=true to confirm all five invariants hold. Rotate to the v2 secret again only when the provider is known to sign with it, or when the receiver accepts both versions during the switch.

diagnosis.blast_radius: The receiver pauses briefly while its container is recreated. Webhooks sent during that pause go unacknowledged and the provider resends them later. If the earlier secret was replaced because it leaked, rolling back reopens that exposure until the rotation is coordinated with the provider. The consumers are idempotent (LEDGER_HANDLER=idempotent, CONFIRMER_HANDLER=by_our_id), so the burst of resent webhooks should not double-book anything. The money check should confirm this.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: Redeploy webhook-receiver with WEBHOOK_SECRET_VERSION=v2. Watch klaxon_webhooks_received_total by result, and keep the rollback only if bad_signature falls to zero and queued recovers.
